pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/lib/pdf/report-document.test.ts:621 The PDF export is asserted only on the near side: element-tree text, plus a non-empty buffer that starts with %PDF-. No test reads the rendered PDF back, so the hard-coded '⚠' at src/lib/pdf/report-document.tsx:115 is pinned as present in the tree (test line 282) even though the repo's own latin1 rule says Helvetica drops glyphs above U+00FF.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/pdf/report-document.test.ts:621 The oracle is the bytes' magic header, not a PDF reader. Text extraction over the rendered buffer would show whether the warning glyph and the latin1Safe output survive.
src/app/api/report/llm/route.test.ts:6 The route test runs the shipped generator rather than a twin, and the header test reads the same function back from the UI end.
src/app/api/report/llm/route.failures.test.ts:39 The 503 mapping is pinned together with the strict-read producer, so a default reader that returns null and yields a 404 cannot pass.

pairs.registryProposal: assert-through-the-reader is written around shells and VCS tools. A binary document format such as PDF, written through a font that cannot encode some glyphs, fits the same law: the claim belongs to the viewer or text extractor. A short note in the technique that document formats are in scope would stop seats from reading the technique as shell-only.
